messages:
kevin: Hey folks, just hit a blocker on day 2. Ran `docker compose up` and postgres container immediately exits with `FATAL: could not create lock file \"/var/lib/postgresql/data/postmaster.pid\": Permission denied`. Using mac + Colima and the compose file has `./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data`. Anyone have a quick fix?

tara: Welcome Kevin! Classic host bind-mount perms issue. Two quick options: switch to a named volume in compose (recommended) or fix permissions on the host folder. Colima sometimes maps ownership weirdly.

kevin: I tried `sudo chown -R 999:999 ./pgdata` but it still dies.

samira: The numeric UID inside the Postgres image is often 999 but on mac/colima user mapping can differ. Try running a temporary container to chown as root inside container: `docker run --rm -v $(pwd)/pgdata:/pgdata --user root alpine sh -c \"chown -R 999:999 /pgdata\"`. If that doesn't work, remove the folder and let compose create the named volume.

ben: Also check for stale lock files. If you previously booted a container it might have created files owned by root. `ls -la ./pgdata` to inspect. If you don't need the data, `rm -rf ./pgdata` and recreate with compose is fastest.

kevin: Ok removed local folder and switched to named volume (`db_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data`). DB stays up now, thanks. One follow-up: my app runs on host (not in container). I left `DATABASE_HOST=db` in .env and it times out. I thought docker compose port mapping would make `db` resolvable from host.

tara: Service names like `db` are only resolvable inside the compose network. For host apps you need to map ports (e.g., `ports: - \"5433:5432\"`) and then connect to `127.0.0.1:5433`. We use 5433 locally to avoid colliding with any system Postgres.

kevin: Ah I was trying localhost:5432 and hitting the host's Postgres. Switched to 5433 and it connects. Thanks.

samira: Quick extra: some people try to use unix sockets (`host=/var/run/postgresql`) when running host app; that socket lives in the container and isn't visible to host. Prefer TCP mapping unless you intentionally run Postgres on host.

ben: Also FYI if you ever need to run Postgres with custom extensions (pgvector etc) in dev, our repo has `docker/postgres/Dockerfile` that adds them. Set `build: ./docker/postgres` on `db` and `docker compose build db` so the extensions are available. Note: `docker-entrypoint-initdb.d` only runs on first init, so you may need to recreate the named volume to trigger init scripts.

kevin: Good to know. One weird edge: I tried to run `docker exec -it <db> psql -U postgres -c \"CREATE EXTENSION vector;\"` and it failed with \"could not open extension control file\". Is rebuilding the image the only way?

samira: Either rebuild image with extension installed, or use the prebuilt image we publish internally `internal-registry.local/local-postgres:14-pgvector` to save time. If you add the extension later, recreate the volume so the `initdb` scripts can create it, or run the SQL after ensuring the extension binary exists in the server.

kevin: Pulled the prebuilt image and migrations ran. All green. Thanks everyone and hi all! :wave:

devex-bot: Welcome Kevin! We've added a short note to onboarding about named volumes vs bind mounts and the 5433 local-port convention. See https://internal.redwood.dev/dev-setup/local-postgres :robot_face:
